title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out with a synthetic video and voice, not a failure of a model to answer a question correctly. The system was deployed against a specific target over a consumer messaging app, in a live call where the victim could see and hear a fabricated public figure. The harm landed at the point of payment, after the impersonation had already done its work.

Catching it would have required the victim to verify the caller through a channel the fraudster did not control, or a platform-level signal that the video was synthetic. Neither is described in the reporting. The amounts demanded, including fees to release aid and a claim to be from an investigating agency, follow a known script for advance-fee fraud, and the deepfake supplied the credibility that script normally lacks.

What is not established is who made the deepfake, what tools were used, or whether anyone has been identified or charged. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act, and a registration is not a finding of guilt.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using a deepfake video and voice to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. The fraudster then demanded fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN, and more than Rs 50,000 from someone claiming to be a CBI officer. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh in total.

Giri refused a further demand of Rs 50,000 and realized he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. A senior officer urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on similar claims.
